info.title: AXLR Bots operator API
info.description: The routes the operator address serves (axlr-bots serve --api-listen), behind the bearer token. The prose reference is operator-api.md. adapters/unixapi/contract_test.go checks this file against the server; panel/tests/operator_contract.rs checks that the panel reads every answer it describes.

What the bots declare, not who is free now

200.description: The group already had an incident: a repeat (no task) or a reopening (a new task), created false

get.description: one incident with needsYou, its current task and the count of its tasks' approvals

post.description: close the incident; a resolved one is 409

approve the postmortem of a resolved incident as who the X-Axlr-Actor header or decidedBy names, naming the text read in authorTaskId; the incident outputs announce it. Refused 403 without a name, under a policy: or trigger: name, a registered bot's id or the daemon's own, or by an actor the approvers of the bot that wrote it do not list; 409 when it is not a Draft, or left to a person with a draft, or holds another text than the one named

send the text read back with a note: its task is launched again; the second send-back of a text leaves it to a person, and a failed task's costs nothing. On a resolved incident with no postmortem of its cycle it asks for one. Who may do it as for approve; a missing note is 400, another text than the one named or a postmortem past the cap is 409

get.description: the incident output targets, in name order; never a URL, a secret or a command, a fingerprint instead

post.description: keep a new incident output target (webhook, slack or command); a name already taken is 409, a definition the control plane refuses 400

delete.description: drop the target and answer what it was; its pending deliveries are skipped; none of that name is 404

post.description: a person marks the diagnosis of the incident's current cycle correct or wrong (X-Axlr-Actor or markedBy names them); 409 when the incident is on no ladder, has no diagnosis this cycle, or was marked the other way

get.description: the runbooks on ladders, by runbook and namespace, with their step, counters and history
one runbook's step, counters and history

post.description: a named person takes the runbook one step down and ends what was outstanding; a task already granted takes the card when it comes to run; 403 for nobody named, a machine or someone not among the apply bot's approvers
a named approver ends the runbook's outstanding applies, lowering and zeroing nothing

autoApprove.description: calls the control plane approves without a person (actor policy:autoApprove)

autoApprove.description: the calls approved without a person: replaces approvals.autoApprove only, the rest of approvals (its notification secrets) stays. Each item is a rule or, for short, a tool name (every call of that tool); the bot keeps rules

oneOf.description: a tool name: the rule with no arguments

decidedBy.description: who decides, as the token holder asserts it (the X-Axlr-Actor header says the same; both given must agree); absent: the control plane's own actor, which a bot that lists approvers, or a call that waits for two persons, refuses with 403

RuntimeSnapshot.description: what runs the bot's tasks on its node: absent or kind axlr for an AXLR session; kind jev for a fixed program whose every decision is one question to Jev, with no language model

JevProgramSnapshot.description: a Jev bot's program: the node's MCP server that serves its tools, the tool that starts a task, how it acts on each of Jev's choices, the tool that waits for the next question, the tool a stop.* task calls, and the pinned Jev model

JevTellSnapshot.description: what a Jev bot tells its teams after each act: the event's name and the fields of the decision that ride as its data (choice, probability, confidence, the act's choice argument, a field passed on; all when none)

JevActSnapshot.description: how a Jev bot acts on a choice: the tool, the argument that takes the choice (its first whole number, else its text), the argument that takes Jev's verdict {choice, probability, confidence}, and the fields of the event's data passed on as they are

fromTeam.description: false: the bot takes no task its teammates delegate; absent: it does

AskSnapshot.description: the other teams the bot may ask for context through the team channel (docs/architecture/team-channel.md); absent: it is not offered the tool

teams.description: the memory teams the bot may ask, at most 8, none of its own

maxOpen.description: questions waiting for an answer at once, 1 to 8; absent: 3

EmitRuleSnapshot.description: one rule of what a bot may emit: a name or pattern (* one segment, ** any); the name's kind (its first segment) fixes the severity

maxSeverity.description: accepted from older definitions and ignored: the kind decides

teams.description: Other teams a domain event of this plain info name crosses to (docs/architecture/team-topics.md).

revoked.description: on a forbidden answer to a node: the node was revoked, and only a fresh enrollment readmits it

groupName.description: the team an event about a team names (group.event.published); such an event names no bot

incidentId.description: the incident an event about an incident names (incident.*); such an event also names the bot that triages it

EventType.description: A client must read a value not listed here as unknown, not refuse the answer: the control plane adds values.

EventsSnapshot.description: what a bot may emit to its teams and how it hears them; absent: any name but error.* and done.*, 6 a minute out, 10 a minute in, chains 2 deep

intakePerMinute.description: how many events the bot takes as tasks or messages in a minute, 1 to 60; past it a delivery is a note; absent: 10

maxDepth.description: how deep a chain an event of the bot starts may go, 1 to 8; absent: 2

interruptible.description: false: no teammate's event interrupts the bot; absent: a critical (danger.*, stop.*) does, and a warning heard by an urgent subscription

ExecutionKind.description: A client must read a value not listed here as unknown, not refuse the answer: the control plane adds values.

ExecutionOutcome.description: A client must read a value not listed here as unknown, not refuse the answer: the control plane adds values.

action.description: an alertmanager or cloudwatch fire: opened, repeated, reopened, resolved or ignored; confirmed for an SNS subscription a cloudwatch trigger confirmed

FireResponse.description: what a fire returns; an alertmanager fire names the incident and what it did to it, and has no task for a repeat, a resolution or a group nobody had

Group.description: a team, derived from the bots that name it in their groups

GroupMember.description: one bot of a team, as its teammates read it in their directory

purpose.description: the first sentence of its mission, at most 120 characters

takesDelegation.description: whether it takes the tasks its teammates delegate

where.description: where its tasks run, in words

GroupLink.description: one link of the team channel: team from may ask team to

askers.description: the bots whose memory team is from and whose ask.teams names to, by id

responders.description: the bots whose memory team is to and whose question trigger's from names from, by id

GroupTopic.description: one topic of a team: who publishes it, who listens and how, the last event

name.description: a name the team's events used, or a pattern its members subscribe to or may emit

publishers.description: who published it, seen in the newest 1000 events: bots, operator, control-plane

declaredPublishers.description: members whose events.emit rules name it

nobodyListens.description: a name published and no member listens to it now, and the last event was not addressed

runtimes.description: the runtimes the node has beside AXLR (jev); absent: AXLR bots only

providers.description: the model providers the node's bots can reach, by name: openrouter, codex, jev, local:<id> per local model its AXLR names; absent: the node did not say (an older node)

memoryTeams.description: the teams whose bots share one KMP store on the node (its --memory-teams), * for every team; absent: none, and the node is never picked to answer a team's question (an older node)

teamChannel.description: the node runs the team channel (axlr-node --team-channel): only then are its runs offered axlr_bots_ask_team and axlr_bots_question_status, its bots picked to answer a team's question, and a team's Jev watcher served; absent: off (the default, and an older node)

allowedTools.description: the tool allow-list the execution was given: the bot's, or its incident phase's, with the node's own tools

PublishAnswer.description: who heard the operator's event and how, who was skipped and why

severity.description: info, warning or critical, fixed by the kind

trigger.description: the subscription it heard the event by, or team

degraded.description: intake_rate: a task or message that became a note

coalescedInto.description: the Pending task the event joined as a note

team.description: the team whose member took the event, picked among the hearers of a team subscription

crossed.description: published to another team, team: its task is made there, so botId and taskId are empty

team.description: team_unavailable: the team of a team subscription nobody could take; botId is empty

crossed.description: not published to another team, team: crossing_limit, no_domain_id, or team_unavailable

PublishGroupEventCommand.description: the operator's event on a team

name.description: a dotted name whose first segment is its kind: stop, danger, warn, info or any other (info)

message.description: one line: what happened and why

data.description: facts for the receivers, at most 8 KiB as JSON

to.description: only these members; absent: the whole team

idempotencyKey.description: the key, when the header carries none

childrenCancelled.description: the delegated tasks it asked other bots for, cancelled

namedBy.description: the other bots that still name it; left as they are

how.description: delegation (its delegation.to names the bot) or subscription (a topic it listens to names the bot in from)

SubscriptionSnapshot.description: one topic a bot listens to in its teams

topic.description: a name or pattern (* one segment, ** any)

mode.description: task, message or note; absent: by the event's severity (info note, warning message, critical task)

from.description: only events of these teammates, operator or control-plane; absent: anyone in the team

urgent.description: true: a warning it hears makes an urgent task

objective.description: the template of the task it makes; absent: who said what

deliver.description: team: one member of the bot's team takes what it hears (mode task only), picked first free by id among the members that say the same

status.description: active (absent) or pending: a bot's ask a person has not approved; a pending subscription hears nothing

team.description: Another team the topic is heard from (docs/architecture/team-topics.md); absent: the bot's own teams.

expects.description: the final events a task it makes must emit, names or patterns (mode task only, never on a bot's ask): for each event the task carried (the one that made it and every one coalesced into it), one event whose name fits and whose data.id is that event's; a carried event without data.id is settled by any of them. What is missing when the task ends is given again in one new task, at most twice per event; then warn.incomplete (docs/architecture/team-subscriptions.md#done-is-a-contract)

eventId.description: set on a task a teammate's event made

priority.description: urgent: go first and cancel the bot's work in progress; absent or normal: wait the turn

incidentId.description: the incident a triage task works on

waiting.example: waiting for node web-1, which is Offline

policy.description: an incident phase's task: the policy its phase narrowed the bot's to, pinned at submission

topics.description: a cloudwatch trigger: the SNS topic ARNs it takes messages from, at most 16; a message of another topic is refused (403). Absent: any topic SNS signed for

severities.description: the postmortem phase's incident trigger: the severities it writes one for, sev1 and sev2 when absent

from.description: a question trigger: the teams whose questions the bot answers, required, at most 8

IncidentSeverity.description: sev1 the worst; absent is sev3. A client must read a value not listed here as unknown.

cycle.description: 1 for the first opening, one more per reopening

tasks.description: the tasks that worked on it, oldest first, each with its bot, phase and cycle: one per phase in each cycle

diagnosis.description: the answer of the last completed triage task

IncidentTaskSnapshot.description: a task that worked on an incident

cycle.description: the incident's cycle it belongs to

events.description: the incident events it hears, full names

TwoPersonsSnapshot.description: the incidents whose calls wait for two different people: those of a namespace or of a severity listed (one match is enough)

authorTaskId.description: the task whose text the person read, as the postmortem's authorTaskId said; empty only when they read none. Another text than the one held now is 409

IncidentPostmortemState.description: where a postmortem is: its task writing it, a draft for a person, sent back or asked for and not launched yet, its task failed, left to a person at the send-back cap, or approved. authorTaskId.description: the task whose answer markdown is

note.description: what the person who last sent it back asked for

reason.description: why its last task did not write it

sendBacks.description: the times a person sent its text back; the second leaves it to a person. Sending back a task that failed does not count

approvedBy.description: who approved it, as the token holder asserted it

AutonomyCounters.description: the three counts a runbook climbs by

AutonomyThresholdsSnapshot.description: how many of each signal a ladder asks for since the last lowering; 0 or absent is the default (5, 10, 20)

AutonomyEntry.description: one signal of a runbook's history; from, to and earnedBefore are present on a step it moved

AutonomyResponse.description: a runbook's standing on its ladder: its step, its counters and its history; saved is false until its first signal comes; diagnosisMark, read through an incident, is the verdict on that incident's diagnosis this cycle

DiagnosisRequest.description: a person's verdict on an incident's diagnosis; who marks it is markedBy or X-Axlr-Actor (both given must agree)

LadderRunbookSnapshot.description: one runbook of a ladder: its alert name, the one write tool it may run alone and the namespaces it may run it in

LadderSnapshot.description: an apply trigger's opt-in to progressive autonomy

PinnedLadderSnapshot.description: the unit of an apply task, whose signals fall on it; alone is what a ladder let it do without a card, maxToolCalls how many calls it may make

AutonomyOutstanding.description: an apply whose end is not recorded: while one is, the runbook gets no grant

LowerRequest.description: a person takes a runbook one step down: who is loweredBy or X-Axlr-Actor (both given must agree), and why

ClearRequest.description: a person ends a runbook's outstanding applies: who is clearedBy or X-Axlr-Actor (both given must agree), and why

EventOrigin.description: Where a task made by another team's domain event came from; such a task starts a new chain (docs/architecture/team-topics.md).

context.description: The KMP key of the event's context, when it named one.

TaskExpectsSnapshot.description: What a task records for its subscription's expects (docs/architecture/team-subscriptions.md#done-is-a-contract).

names.description: the names or patterns a final event fits

carried.description: the events the task carries, oldest first: the one that made it and those coalesced into it

finals.description: the events the task emitted that settled a carried one

CarriedEvent.description: One event a task carries for its subscription's expects.

id.description: its data.id (a number in its shortest form); absent when it had none

redeliveries.description: how many times the control plane gave it again

tasks.description: the earlier tasks that carried it, oldest first

FinalEvent.description: An event a task emitted that settled an event it carried.

revision.description: the commit the binary was built from (vcs.revision); absent for a build without version control

BuildStatus.description: The build the control plane runs, the one installed on its disk, and whether the running one is stale: a newer binary was installed and the service was not restarted (the daemon then stops itself within its check period).

reason.description: why nothing could be compared, when that is the case
